clue.text: Free nude in arrest, surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters of these three words turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A naked person apparently released while being arrested, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something free is not held back or restricted in any way.

clue.text: A French bloke eats high-class cream

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the word for bloke takes in, or consumes, the next piece

parts.note: a gent is a man or bloke
U stands for upper-class, a long-standing British label

explanation.surface: A Frenchman tucks into a posh dessert cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like food in the surface, but it is the ointment sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ointment or salve rubbed onto skin is a medicinal cream.

clue.text: Posh car carrying Queen giving waves

indicators.note: the car's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a Rolls (Rolls-Royce) is the classic luxury car
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A luxury car with the monarch aboard, who waves to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' seems to be the Queen's royal wave; it is the noun for big sea swells.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: long heavy breakers rolling in from the sea are called rollers.

clue.text: Still in garden in sun before day's end

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come ahead of the final letter
the word for garden sits inside the word for sun

parts.note: the sun is a star
Eden is the biblical garden

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Sitting motionless in the garden, sunbathing until the day draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sedentary person stays put, inactive and seated, much as someone still does not move.

clue.text: Others without beginning of idea take test again

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the word for others goes around the next piece

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The other students, lacking any idea, must sit the exam once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a student who failed an examination sits it once more.

clue.text: 'Chin-chin' — gently swallows going slowly

indicators.note: the words take the answer down inside them, hiding it in the letters

explanation.surface: A toast is made, and the drinker sips gently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: moving forward bit by bit, a small distance at a time, is going slowly.

clue.text: See mine blowing up foes

indicators.note: the letters explode and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Watch a mine explode under the opposing army.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hostile opponents or adversaries are foes.

clue.text: Copier prints erratically — instruction needed

indicators.note: the letters come out in an irregular, jumbled order

explanation.surface: The photocopier is printing badly, so a manual is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a doctor's written direction for medicine is an instruction to the pharmacist.

clue.text: Amused lass in grass

indicators.note: the word for lass sits inside the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a gal is a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl lying in the long grass is entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to entertain someone with stories is to amuse them.

clue.text: Extract offspring vocally expressing triumph

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken aloud and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: to extract is to suck, and offspring are seed, giving suck seed

explanation.surface: Getting children out and shouting about the victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to triumph is to win through or be successful.

clue.text: Dines with a select spread from here?

definitions.text: Dines with a select spread from here?

indicators.note: the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eats a choice buffet bought at a fancy shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a select spread may well come from such a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and fine foods is where a choice buffet might be bought.

clue.text: Illicit boozer's brilliance hiding empty bottle

indicators.note: the word for brilliance conceals the next piece within it

parts.note: sheen is a shine or brilliance

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sparkle at an unlicensed bar conceals a drained bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish and Scottish word for an unlicensed drinking den, an illegal pub.

clue.text: Petty and oddly vain during rehearsal

indicators.note: the odd letters come within the word for rehearsal

parts.note: a trial is a test run or rehearsal

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: An actor is small-minded and conceited at the practice run.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something petty is minor and unimportant.

clue.text: Reportedly composes ceremonies

indicators.note: as heard in speech, the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: to compose a text is to write it

explanation.surface: A headline: someone apparently writes ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: formal religious or solemn rituals are ceremonies.

clue.text: Painkiller that could produce endlessly calm easing

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged to produce something new
the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A pain remedy that brings on calm and relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims calm to CAL; CAL plus EASING is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a drug that relieves pain, such as aspirin, is a painkiller.

clue.text: Garden is completely excessive, with chaps digging in

parts.note: all means wholly or completely

indicators.note: the word for chaps burrows inside the word for excessive

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A garden thoroughly overdone, with men out working the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented British garden plot, often for vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of rented land for growing vegetables is a kind of garden.

clue.text: Representation from Left facing abuse, some say

indicators.note: the phrase as spoken by some sounds like the answer

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, and to rail is to abuse verbally, giving port rail

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the left wing confronts insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a depiction of someone in art or acting is a representation of them.

clue.text: Give new name for party in spin

indicators.note: the party sits inside the word for spin

parts.note: to reel is to spin around
Lab is short for Labour, the UK political party

explanation.surface: A political party rebrands itself through spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: to put a fresh tag on something is to rename it.

clue.text: Pull up in back, as frequent pub-goer

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: to lug is to haul or pull

explanation.surface: Pulling a pint in the back room for a familiar customer.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer who comes to the same bar often is known there as one of the usuals.

clue.text: Discretion accepting one's understood

indicators.note: the word for discretion takes the next piece in

parts.note: tact is discretion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Discretion allowing that someone's meaning is grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tacit is implied rather than spoken, so understood without being said.

clue.text: Minister: 'Ministry includes transport depots'

indicators.note: the words contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A minister announces that the department covers bus and rail stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: end stations of bus or rail lines are depots for transport.

clue.text: Revolutionary radical's cigar

parts.note: Che Guevara is the famous revolutionary
radical comes from Latin for root

explanation.surface: The cigar belonging to a radical revolutionary, perhaps Castro's.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cheroot is a kind of cigar cut square at both ends.

clue.text: Criminal in trouble, say, famous gangster

parts.note: ill means in a bad way, in trouble
say means for example, abbreviated eg
Al Capone was the famous gangster

explanation.surface: A crook in difficulty, perhaps a notorious mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anything criminal is against the law.

clue.text: Weighed down and left a hole

parts.note: a den is a lair or hole

explanation.surface: Burdened, someone departed and left a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something laden is loaded heavily, so burdened.

clue.text: Goes off eating ends of edible dishes

indicators.note: the word for goes off takes in the next piece

parts.note: milk turns when it goes off

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Food spoiling as someone eats from plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: deep serving bowls for soup are a type of dish.

clue.text: Fat cat, exhausted, getting collared

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy, upper-class person, like a fat cat
bled dry means exhausted of resources

explanation.surface: A wealthy boss, worn out, being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: nobbled can mean caught or grabbed, as being collared means being seized.

clue.text: Record, single, needs volume for example

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a tome is a large book or volume

explanation.surface: Music talk: a record and a single need a volume, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model or typical specimen is the ideal example of something.

clue.text: Musician's recital isn't ruined by tenor initially

indicators.note: the next letter is placed alongside, beside the rearranged letters
the letters are wrecked into a new order
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A performer's concert is not spoiled by the tenor at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who plays a woodwind instrument in an orchestra is a musician.
